class.name: PhysXDustDevils3D
class.brief_description: Dust devils over hot, dry ground, drawn in NVIDIA Flow.
class.description: Spawns convective vortices round [member follow_target] at a rate set by the weather: the surface's heating over the air, light wind, sunshine, dry ground and no rain (read from the world's weather through [WorldContracts]), where the ground's dust is loose (WorldGround blown sand). Each one drifts with the wind for a few minutes and is drawn in a [PhysXFlow3D] of its own: rings of air-only emitters spin the column and draw air in at the foot, a warm core lifts it, and the foot ring lifts the dust, which Flow carries up the wall and fans out on top.

method.name: get_devil
method.description: Devil [param index] among the living ones: its ground position (x, z), its swirl ring radius in metres, and its swirl speed now in m/s (zero while it spins up or dies away). Zero past [method get_devil_count].

method.name: get_favour
method.description: How favourable the weather is round [member follow_target], 0 to 1, from the last physics frame.

method.name: get_favour_at
method.description: How favourable the weather is at [param position], 0 to 1: the surface's heating over the air past [member min_heating], times a light wind, dry ground and sun. 0 in rain or without a weather provider.

method.name: get_flow
method.description: The [PhysXFlow3D] this node made, to tune its look (cell size, density, scattering).

method.name: get_spawned
method.description: Devils formed since the node entered the tree, by the weather or by [method spawn].

method.name: spawn
method.description: Forms a devil at [param position] (on the ground there), with a swirl ring of [param radius] metres and [param swirl] m/s on it; below 0, drawn at random as the weather's own. Returns its index for [method get_devil], or -1 when [member max_devils] are alive.

members.member: The dust's per-scatter tint: Flow weighs each scatter by this colour times the scattering albedo (0.97), so the column's tan comes from many scatters inside it. Desert dust: about 0.97 red, 0.93 green, 0.86 blue (Dubovik et al. 2002). A darker colour darkens the dense foot fast.
Off: no new devils, and the living ones die away within 25 seconds.

The Flow grid's cell size in metres. Smaller cells show finer swirls at more GPU cost and fill the grid's block budget (2048) sooner: at 0.25 the column and its drifting trail asked for over 1,800 blocks within 8 s.
Centre of the area where devils form. Empty: the viewport's camera.
Devils formed per square kilometre per hour at full favour.
Devils alive at once (each costs Flow time while it lives).
Kelvin of the surface over the air below which none form; the favour is full 12 K above it.
Seed of the spawning and the devils' sizes and wander.
Radius round [member follow_target] where devils form; one drifting past twice this is dropped.
The terrain the dust rests on (the Flow floor, [member PhysXFlow3D.terrain_path]).
